text: One day Paul, the only son. <break time="0.8s" /> Asked his mother. <break time="0.8s" /> Why they did not keep a car of their own. <break time="0.8s" /> And why they always used Uncles car. <break time="0.8s" /> Or else a taxi. <break time="0.8s" /> Because we are the poorest members. <break time="0.8s" /> Of the family. <break time="0.8s" /> Said the mother. <break time="0.8s" /> And when Paul asked why. <break time="0.8s" /> She answered bitterly. <break time="0.8s" /> That it was because his father had no luck. <break time="0.8s" /> Is luck money, mother. <break time="0.8s" /> He asked. <break time="0.8s" /> And she explained. <break time="0.8s" /> That luck was what caused you to have money. <break time="0.8s" /> So it was better to be born lucky. <break time="0.8s" /> Than rich. <break time="0.8s" /> When the boy asked. <break time="0.8s" /> Whether she herself was lucky. <break time="0.8s" /> She said. <break time="0.8s" /> That she used to think so. <break time="0.8s" /> Before she married. <break time="0.8s" /> But that now she believed. <break time="0.8s" /> She was very unlucky indeed. <break time="0.8s" /> The child looked at her. <break time="0.8s" /> With unsure eyes. <break time="0.8s" /> Then said stoutly. <break time="0.8s" /> Well, anyhow, I am a lucky person. <break time="0.8s" /> And when she asked why. <break time="0.8s" /> He answered, God told me. <break time="0.8s" /> He saw. <break time="0.8s" /> That she did not believe him. <break time="0.8s" /> Or rather. <break time="0.8s" /> That she paid no attention to his words. <break time="0.8s" /> And this angered him. <break time="0.8s" /> And made him want. <break time="0.8s" /> To compel her attention. <break time="0.8s" /> He went off by himself. <break time="0.8s" /> Searching for the clue to luck. <break time="0.8s" /> And he would sit. <break time="0.8s" /> On his big rocking horse. <break time="0.8s" /> Charging madly into space. <break time="0.8s" /> With a frenzy that made his little sisters uneasy. <break time="0.8s" /> Now he would silently command the snorting steed. <break time="0.8s" /> Now, take me to where there is luck. <break time="0.8s" /> And he would strike its neck. <break time="0.8s" /> With his little whip. <break time="0.8s" /> When he finally slid down. <break time="0.8s" /> He announced fiercely. <break time="0.8s" /> Well, I got there. <break time="0.8s" /> And when his mother asked where. <break time="0.8s" /> He flared back. <break time="0.8s" /> Where I wanted to go.
